source_text:
Τηνικαῦτα δέ φησι· ὁ Κύριος εἶπεν αὐτῇ· δύο ἔθνη ἐν τῇ γαστρί σού εἰσιν, καὶ δύο λαοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας σου
διασταλήσονται, καὶ λαὸς λαοῦ ὑπερέξει, καὶ ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι. Πολλὰ μὲν γὰρ ἔθνη καὶ πολλοὶ τυγχάνουσι λαοὶ, δύο δὲ τούτους ἐξαιρέτως ὀνομάζουσι λαοὺς, οἳ τὸ δόγμα τῆς εὐσεβείας ἐγχειρισθῆναι κατηξιώθησαν, –οὔτε δὲ σχισμάτων, οὔτε αἱρέσεων, οὔτε ἐναριθμίων μέμνηται–ἀλλὰ δύο μέν εἰσι λαοὶ πολλαχοῦ γῆς ἐκτεταμένοι, Χριστιανῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων. Ὁ δὲ μείζων τοῖς χρόνοις αὐχῶν εἶναι, λειπόμενος ἀρετῇ δουλεύσει τῷ νεωτέρῳ· δουλεύσεται γὰρ ἄφρων, ἔφη, φρονίμῳ. 9 Ἐντεῦθεν τοίνυν ἐπὶ θρόνου προὔγραφεν αὐτὸν τοῦ ἁγίου καθέζεσθαι, δηλῶν ὅτι σύνθρονος ἀποδέδεικται τῷ θειοτάτῳ Πνεύματι διὰ τὸν οἰκοῦντα Θεὸν ἐν αὐτῷ διηνεκῶς.
thought_title: The Two Peoples and the Younger's Dominion
orientation: Eustathius is closing his treatise by interpreting the Lord's words to Rebecca about the two nations in her womb as a prophecy of Jews and Christians, with the older people serving the younger.
pass_a_gloss: Then he says: The Lord said to her: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from your belly will be separated, and people will surpass people, and the greater will serve the lesser. For many nations and many peoples happen to exist, but they name these two exceptionally peoples, who were deemed worthy to be entrusted with the teaching of piety, —and he mentions neither schisms, nor heresies, nor those counted among them—but there are two peoples stretched out over many parts of the earth, of Christians and of Jews. And the greater, boasting to be in times, being left behind in virtue, will serve the younger; for the fool, he said, will serve the wise. From there, then, he wrote beforehand that he sits upon the throne of the holy one, making clear that he has been shown to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because of the God dwelling in him perpetually.

Fixed glossary term for the two peoples from Rebecca's womb.
Renders δόγμα as teaching and εὐσέβεια as piety, preserving the doctrinal sense.

choices.why: Preserves the infinitive construction and the literal 'throne of the holy one'.

pass_b_english: Then he says: The Lord said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from your body; one people will surpass the other, and the greater will serve the lesser” (Genesis 25:23). For there are many nations and many peoples, but these two in particular are called peoples, because they were deemed worthy to be entrusted with the teaching of piety. He makes no mention of schisms or heresies or those that would be numbered. Rather, there are two peoples stretched out across much of the earth: Christians and Jews. The greater, boasting in its antiquity, is left behind in virtue and will serve the younger; for, as Scripture says, “the fool will serve the wise”. From this, then, he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One, showing that he has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because God dwells in him continually.

problems.quote: he wrote beforehand that he sits upon the throne of the Holy One
problems.source_quote: ἐπὶ θρόνου προὔγραφεν αὐτὸν τοῦ ἁγίου καθέζεσθαι
problems.why: προὔγραφεν means 'portrayed/drew beforehand' or 'prefigured', not 'wrote beforehand'; also 'τοῦ ἁγίου' is 'of the saint/holy one' but context suggests 'the Holy One' as divine title. The subject of καθέζεσθαι is ambiguous but 'he sits' seems to refer to Jacob/Christ.
problems.fix: he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One

problems.quote: He makes no mention of schisms or heresies or anything of that kind.
problems.source_quote: οὔτε δὲ σχισμάτων, οὔτε αἱρέσεων, οὔτε ἐναριθμίων μέμνηται
problems.why: ἐναριθμίων means 'those to be numbered/counted,' not 'anything of that kind.' The source says schisms, heresies, and those to be numbered are not mentioned.
problems.fix: He makes no mention of schisms or heresies or those that would be numbered.
problems.ruling: ἐναριθμίων is a specific term meaning 'counted/numbered ones,' not vague 'anything of that kind.' Meaning lost.

problems.quote: showing that he has been shown enthroned together with the most divine Spirit
problems.source_quote: δηλῶν ὅτι σύνθρονος ἀποδέδεικται τῷ θειοτάτῳ Πνεύματι
problems.why: ἀποδέδεικται means 'has been shown/demonstrated,' not 'has been shown enthroned.' The compound σύνθρονος already means 'enthroned together'; adding it again is redundant and confusing.
problems.fix: showing that he has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit
problems.ruling: ἀποδέδεικται means 'has been shown/demonstrated,' not 'shown enthroned.' σύνθρονος already carries 'enthroned together.'

fixed: Removed the incorrect scripture citation for 'the fool will serve the wise'; the source does not identify a specific verse, and the saying matches no standard verse.

problems.quote: From this, then, he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One
problems.why: Unclear who 'he' is (Jacob? Eustathius? the Lord?) and who 'him' is (Christ? Jacob?).
problems.fix: Clarify: 'From this oracle, Jacob prefigured Christ sitting...'

problems.quote: showing that he has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because God dwells in him continually
problems.why: Unclear who 'he' refers to—Christ? Jacob? The Holy Spirit?
problems.fix: Specify 'showing that Christ has been demonstrated...'

problems.quote: the fool will serve the wise
problems.why: Quoted as Scripture but no citation given; seems to mash up Proverbs with Genesis oracle.
problems.fix: Add source or rephrase as Eustathius's inference.

problems.quote: he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One
problems.why: 'Holy One' usually refers to God, but here seems to mean the Holy Spirit; confusing.
problems.fix: 'throne of the Most Holy' or clarify Spirit reference.

problems.quote: From this, then, he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One, showing that he has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because God dwells in him continually.
problems.why: Ambiguous pronouns: 'he' and 'him' could refer to Jacob, Christ, or the younger people.
problems.fix: Clarify whether 'he' is Jacob prefiguring Christ, and 'him' is Christ.

problems.why: 'Left behind in virtue' is unclear; likely means 'surpassed in virtue' or 'falls short in virtue.'
problems.fix: Use 'falls short in virtue' or 'is surpassed in virtue.'

edits.old: From this, then, he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One, showing that he has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because God dwells in him continually.
edits.new: From this oracle, then, Jacob prefigured Christ sitting upon the throne of the Holy One, showing that Christ has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because God dwells in him continually.

edits.old: for, as Scripture says, “the fool will serve the wise”.
edits.new: for, as Scripture says, “the fool will serve the wise” (Proverbs 11:29).

fixed: The pronoun ambiguity in the final sentence is resolved by specifying Jacob as the one prefiguring and Christ as the one enthroned.
The phrase 'is left behind in virtue' is clarified to 'falls short in virtue' to convey the sense of being surpassed.
The quotation 'the fool will serve the wise' is given a citation to Proverbs 11:29, matching the Septuagint wording.

last_rejected.ruling: ἄφρων/φρονίμῳ correctly rendered 'fool/wise'; no λαοί term present here to gloss.

last_rejected.why: Source marks this as Proverbs quotation per voices; English hides speaker attribution.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔφη means 'he said'; 'as Scripture says' is reasonable since author quotes Scripture.
